what: Builder ran many repeated source searches (ls/grep/sed on catalog and CLI output) without calling kb_search; the guard warned seven times.
why: Builder defaulted to reading CLI output and source instead of kb-first discipline required by the standing rules.
workaround: Builder continued; later kb_search calls were made.

what: CLI query of TwoWayRelationMember failed: asking for field partner without a sub-selection returns SubselectionRequired.
why: The query select syntax needs a nested selection for ref fields; builder did not know the syntax.
workaround: Builder queried fqn and primary only and used validate output instead.

what: Validator error AllRequiredFeaturesHaveBindingIfCreatable: a transfer object used by a create operation excludes required features (ProductInfo lacked sku and unit).
why: Required features on a create-used transfer object must be bound (MAPPED) to the entity; builder had not added them.
workaround: Added MAPPED DataMembers sku and unit with binding to Product features, then validate passed.

what: Validator error AggregationOnBothSidesAreNotAllowed (circular aggregation) on the mapped one-way relations ProductInfo.category and CategoryInfo.products, which the CLI created with relationKind AGGREGATION by default.
why: Both ends of the pair defaulted to AGGREGATION; builder did not know the default or the rule for one-way mapped relations.
workaround: Set both relationKind to ASSOCIATION so validate passed; later set ProductInfo.category back to AGGREGATION (only one side) to get the autocomplete form widget.

what: judo create -t MenuItemAccess is refused: the menu item access is created automatically with the actor access.
why: Menu item accesses are generated by the Designer cascade, not by a direct create command.
workaround: Used create -t Access on the actor and let the cascade create the menu item.

what: Validator warned: columns are not defined for a viewable table with a target on ProductInfo.category.
why: A relation feature on a table needs its columns defined; builder had not yet defined them.
workaround: Added name column to the category relation in the form and view.

what: update --feature name failed on CategoryInfo and ProductInfo: name is not a placeable feature on the table or view element because the feature is on the nested relation.
why: Builder targeted the wrong element; the feature belongs to the nested category or products relation.
workaround: Targeted the nested element instead (CategoryInfo_View_Edit products column).

what: Maven validate and build print systemPath errors for com.sun:tools (tools.jar not absolute) in the generated build log, on every build; BUILD SUCCESS is still printed.
why: Generated pom uses a relative tools.jar path; the build still reported BUILD SUCCESS.
workaround: Noted only; build succeeded.

what: Builder ran a bare tsc command that is not the project compiler; the tool printed a wrong-command banner.
why: Builder ran a command outside the project toolchain.
workaround: Builder moved on to the build script.

what: Category shown on the catalog card through a nested mask {name,price,description,sku,category{name}} in the list call, with a Chip for the category and a caption for the SKU.
why: A nested mask returns the related category name in one list call; no extra request per card.

what: Seed data built through the UI helpers (fillEnumCombobox, fillSingleRelationElement) in helpers-shop.ts: 3 categories and 8 products via real user actions.
why: Checks and seeding must use real user actions only; the e2e helpers encode the Playwright patterns.

what: Seed test failed with a 500: column t02.c_sku does not exist in the persistent PostgreSQL database after SKU was added to the model.
why: A stored member added to a persistent database needs a schema-upgrade; the builder assumed the generated changelog would apply to the existing volume.
workaround: Builder removed the postgres and keycloak containers and volumes, restarted, and reseeded the dev user.

what: ./judo.sh schema-upgrade failed with Non-readable POM for the schema directory; with -o schema_dir=application it ran for 900 seconds and timed out.
why: The schema-upgrade step expects a schema module directory and a running persistent DB; the default layout did not match this project and the run hung.
workaround: Killed the run and reset the database volumes instead of upgrading.

what: Playwright fill() on the generated text field did not store the value; the create dialog stayed open and Create was never accepted. Stored data then failed with MISSING_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTE on categories create.
why: Generated inputs store the value on blur or on real key events, not on programmatic fill().
workaround: Used pressSequentially with a blur after each field.

what: Create button locator with exact regex /^Create$/ did not match the dialog button; the test waited 10 seconds and failed.
why: The accessible name of the button differs from the label used in the test.
workaround: Changed the locator to /Create$/.

what: Seed test looked for catalog-grid and then for a generic no-rows text; both locators were guessed, and the test failed on each before it matched the real markup.
why: The builder guessed selectors instead of reading the e2e locator conventions.
workaround: Replaced locators with or() alternatives and the table row locator.

what: Builder tried representationComponent link, autocomplete and tag on the category relation; the CLI accepted only table (then button after relationKind changed). The catalog lists table, button and tag for to-one relations.
why: Allowed representationComponent values depend on relationKind as enforced by the CLI, which the catalog's shape table does not state clearly; the builder guessed values before reading the catalog.
workaround: Set relationKind to AGGREGATION on ProductInfo.category, then set representationComponent to table on Form and View_Edit.

what: Relation widget on the product form rendered as a link button; the builder wanted a dropdown picker for the category and found that a dropdown is a separate widget (isTypeAheadField/autocompleteRows), not a representationComponent value.
why: The mapping of to-one relation to widget is split across attributes and the catalog pages disagree on which values apply.
workaround: Kept the table representation and used the existing relation selector in the form.

what: Seed helper passed the dialog as the locator for the Unit and Category pickers; their option popups render outside the dialog, so the option click timed out, and the relation waited on a range response that never came.
why: The popup rendered outside the dialog scope; the builder scoped the locator to the dialog.
workaround: Opened the combobox in the dialog and clicked the option from the page scope; used pressSequentially for the category.

what: Create-rename-delete test failed on a strict-mode violation: two grid cells named Temp Shoes from earlier failed runs.
why: The test used a fixed name and was not idempotent; leftovers from previous runs stayed in the database.
workaround: Made the name unique with Date.now() and added a cleanup of leftover Temp categories in the seed.

what: Sort-by-price test read prices from all table rows, including the 0 row and a non-selected row, so the expected order was wrong.
why: Row selector matched every row instead of the data rows.
workaround: Limited the selector to rows with aria-selected.

what: Footwear products test expected Wool socks to be absent, but the earlier data left it in the list; the test depended on state from other runs.
why: Test data is not isolated per run and the expectation assumed a clean list.
workaround: Changed the seed to remove leftovers and reran the suite; the suite then passed.

what: Table filters defaulted to labels such as NameFilter, so the test could not find the Name filter in the menu.
why: The DataFilter label is not set by default from the attribute; the catalog does not say so.
workaround: Set labels Name, SKU, Unit and Price (number) on the filters with update -s label=.

what: kb_get returned not found for section paths that kb_search had just returned (agent-docs/e2e-testing/model-screen-layout.md and agent-docs/frontend/esm-to-ui-mappings/widgets.md); builder then read the files by grep.
why: The kb_get path or heading lookup failed for paths that exist; the builder's TRACE also says platform-behavior-reference.md was not found by kb_get.
workaround: Read the files directly with awk and grep, and noted the miss in TRACE.md.

what: Two price columns in the admin table: Price (numeric) and a formatted Price label, so the tests can tell them apart.
why: Numeric sort and labelled price need different columns; the test selects the numeric one by its label.

what: Category entity, CategoryInfo transfer object, categories access (create, update, delete), Categories menu, generated table, form and view; commit 836c3d6.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: sku (SKU type with regExp and maxLength 20), unit (Unit enumeration PIECE/KG/LITRE), and a category relation on Product; shown in product form, view and table; commit 836c3d6.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: name and sku and unit required (required=true); save without SKU shows Missing required attribute.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: sku as identifier attribute on Product; duplicate SKU rejected in create dialog, dialog stays open with error.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: SKU type regExp ^[A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{4}$ and maxLength 20; ab1234 rejected.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: Unit enumeration with PIECE, KG, LITRE; form dropdown shows 3 options.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: Product table with Name, SKU, Unit, Price and Price (number) columns, filters Name, SKU, Unit, Price (number), numeric sort and paging tests.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: Product.category and Category.products as a two-way relation (ASSOCIATION both ends); category view lists its products, product links back to category.
why: Level 1 batch.

what: Builder built the category view with a Products button that opens a list instead of an embedded table on the view, which FUNCTIONS.md asks for.
why: Builder chose a button representation and did not follow the table-on-view pattern from the catalog.
workaround: Round 7 correction: switched to an inline table on the view (see c03-40).

what: kb_get returned not found for an agent-docs/model/ui-authoring-guide.md section that kb_search had just returned.
why: Same kb_get lookup failure as earlier in the round; section heading lookup does not match.
workaround: Used grep and sed on the catalog file.

what: kb_search for eager or isEager and embedded tables on views returned generic embedded-table sections; the view-table example (TabularReferenceField with representationComponent=table) was only found by grep, and no isEager attribute exists in the catalog.
why: The orchestrator's term isEager is not a catalog concept; the catalog answer is the to-many TabularReferenceField on the view, which the search did not rank first.
workaround: Read the catalog by grep, then used a to-many TabularReferenceField with representationComponent table on the view.

what: Builder noted that the CLI lists table, button, tag and card as valid representationComponent values for a to-many relation, while the catalog shape table lists table, card and tag only.
why: Possible mismatch between the catalog shape table and the CLI schema for to-many relations.

what: Builder checked the catalog for how users get created and found a managed-actor admin pattern and a multi-actor projection blueprint; no documented first-login user creation without custom code.
why: Catalog authentication guide says first-login insert must be done by an AuthenticationInterceptor until a release auto-inserts it (agent-docs/backend/authentication-guide.md).

what: Builder noted that an image stored as a binary attribute cannot be used as a plain img src, because the download needs the token header; the catalog says to use a binary-to-object-URL hook.
why: Catalog states the download path is a separate authenticated request and marks the src behaviour as verify for the generated version.
workaround: Planned to use the object-URL hook for image display, with a placeholder when there is no image.

what: Category Products shown as an inline to-many table on CategoryInfo View_Edit (representationComponent=table, with name, sku, priceLabel, unit columns) instead of the Products button, as the Round 7 correction asks.
why: FUNCTIONS.md asks for an embedded table; a to-many relation on a view renders as an embedded table in the catalog pattern.

what: Product image modelled as a BinaryType ProductImage (mime types image/png and image/jpeg, max 2 MB) on a STORED Product.image member.
why: Binary types need a MIME list and a size limit; the attachment blueprint says a binary field on a create-capable transfer gets a generated upload operation.

what: Rename the actor Shop to Customer and the entity ShopUser to CustomerAccount with email as the claim attribute, keeping the mapped principal transfer object; the Admin actor is the second actor.
why: Actor split needs distinct actors with their own principals and accesses; rename keeps the existing wiring.

what: graphql and CLI queries used Claim name or a claim fqn that does not exist (Customer username USERNAME, Claim name field); the query or update failed.
why: Builder assumed the Claim type has a name field; the schema does not expose it under that name.
workaround: Queried Claim fqn only.

what: Renaming the username member to email with a new type left the mapped member on the actor info transfer object with the old type; validate warned the data type must match its binding.
why: A rename plus type change must be applied to the mapped member too; the builder changed only the entity side first.
workaround: Renamed the mapped member in the same script step.

what: The Round 7 model script applied many CLI edits in one run with no check between steps; a partial run left unsaved edits, so the builder discarded them and reran the script.
why: CLI edits are applied one at a time, and a failing step does not roll back the earlier ones.
workaround: Ran discard --force, then reran the script from a clean model.

what: Stock status is a DERIVED string with a ternary getter (stock <= 0 gives Out of stock, below 5 gives Low, else In stock); category name is a DERIVED flattening self.category.name.
why: Derived attributes compute from the model without storing; ternary getters are typed switch expressions in JQL.

what: Transfer objects created with a mapping (VariantInfo, AddressInfo, AdminAccountInfo) already had mapped members; adding the same members again gave BindingIsNotMappedByOtherMappedAttribute and NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer errors. Adding a label feature that is not placeable also failed.
why: Creating a TransferObjectType with a mapping auto-creates the mapped members; the builder's script added them a second time. The CLI reference does not say so.
workaround: Deleted the duplicate DataMembers and kept the auto-created ones.

what: Admin actor added as a second actor with its own principal AdminAccountInfo (managed=false), branding copied from the shop, an EMAIL claim, products and categories accesses, and two menu entries.
why: Each actor needs its own principal, claim and accesses; the Admin keeps the back office and the Customer keeps the shop.

what: Creating an actor with a principal auto-creates a Claim per attribute (for example Customer email USERNAME and EMAIL); the builder removed the USERNAME claim so only EMAIL remains.
why: The principal and claim cascade in the CLI creates claims by default; the catalog does not say which claim to keep.
workaround: Deleted the USERNAME claim on Customer.

what: Email is shown read-only for customers by making the email field enabledBy a derived Boolean that is always false.
why: The model has no direct read-only flag for one field in one view; enabledBy on a derived Boolean is the documented visibility or enablement rule.

what: After generate alone the new webshop__customer and webshop__admin modules had no src/custom folder; it appeared only after the build. The catalog does not say when src/custom is created.
why: Generation creates the module shell; the custom folder and hook scaffolds come from the build step, which the catalog does not state.
workaround: Read the generated tree; no custom code moved yet; decision deferred to the frontend step.

what: ctx_execute ran with /bin/sh and failed on bash process substitution syntax.
why: The shell used for the sandbox does not support process substitution.
workaround: Re-ran the command without process substitution.

what: Builder read the generated LogAuthenticationInterceptor.java.default scaffold, the interceptors module, to plan the first-login user insert.
why: Catalog says managed actor auto-insert is not implemented in the runtime, so a custom AuthenticationInterceptor is needed.

what: Several Round 7 steps read generated Java and TypeScript (sdk, internal, frontend services, ImageDisplay) with grep and python without a prior kb_search; the standing rule says the kb comes first and the gap must be logged.
why: Builder went to generated code directly to learn the DAO, query and image APIs and did not log a kb miss in GAPS.md.
workaround: Used the generated API it found; no GAPS entry was made for the lookup at that point.

what: Customer account created on first login by a custom AuthenticationInterceptor (CustomerProvisioningInterceptor) in the interceptors module; admin accounts are seeded on purpose, not created on login.
why: Runtime does not auto-insert the managed principal row, so a first-login interceptor is the documented route; interceptors module is custom code, not a generated file.

what: The model has no setting for Keycloak self sign-up (registrationAllowed); the generated realm JSON leaves it unset, so the builder had to set it through the Keycloak admin API.
why: The platform's generated realm does not expose a self sign-up switch in the documented model settings; catalog does not cover it.
workaround: Logged as GAPS R7-3; the seed script switches self sign-up on through the Keycloak admin API.

what: Generated actor modules (webshop__admin, webshop__customer) each get their own e2e module; the Level 0 Playwright tests had to be split across them by hand (git mv).
why: Each actor has its own generated e2e and frontend module; the catalog does not say how existing tests move between them.
workaround: Moved helpers and specs to the matching module, changed the base URL to Admin or Customer, and added actor-specific login helpers.

what: Playwright could not install chromium on this machine (it hangs on extraction), so the local config uses the installed Chrome channel and no retries.
why: Environment problem with the browser download, not a JUDO issue.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts sets channel chrome, workers 1, retries 0.

what: Seed script creates Keycloak users admin, customer1 and customer2, switches realm self sign-up on through the admin API, and seeds one AdminAccount row; customer rows are left to the first-login interceptor.
why: Keycloak users and database rows are two stores; sign-up needs a realm setting the model cannot express.

what: Level 0 webshop__shop frontend and e2e modules were removed from git and disk; their code was split into webshop__customer (shop front) and webshop__admin (back office) modules, with duplicated Price, CatalogHome and hook files.
why: The Customer actor takes over the shop front, the Admin takes the CRUD screens, and each actor has its own generated module.

what: Builder added src/custom/application-customizer.tsx to .generator-ignore in the admin and customer frontend modules, against the standing rule that .generator-ignore entries are never added.
why: The only documented registration point is a generated file; the R1-3 exception was approved only for the shop module, and the builder applied it to two new modules.
workaround: Left the entries in place; not reverted in this chunk.

what: Seed upload through the generated binary input: setInputFiles set the file name in the textbox, but the test looked for an img inside the dialog and timed out.
why: The generated BinaryTypeInput shows the file name in a text field, not an image; the test expectation was wrong for the generated widget.
workaround: Asserted the textbox value img-SKU.png after upload.

what: judo-cli.jar was missing from target/ after generate and build steps, so CLI calls failed with Unable to access jarfile; the builder had to run generate-root to restore it.
why: Cause not stated in the session; the target folder was gone after a build step.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root before each CLI session that followed a generate.

what: Admin details page shows Price before Name and Description; the field order test failed, so the builder marked it test.fail() with a reason.
why: Generated view orders the number widget before the text widgets; same platform bug as the create form.
workaround: test.fail() with reason; the customer front has its own details layout that fixes the order.

what: Category products test found Running shoe twice (in the category view table and the product list), so the locator was ambiguous.
why: Same product shown in two grids on the page; locator was not scoped to the table.
workaround: Scoped the locator to the row and used exact name matching.

what: Admin product view cannot show the stored image: the generated binary field is an upload control that shows the file name, so the image test on the admin view was changed to check the file name.
why: The generated admin binary widget is an upload field; a picture view needs a custom display, which the customer front provides.
workaround: Admin test asserts the file name; the customer front shows the image through the generated ImageDisplay path.

what: Variant create dialog had no SKU textbox when the builder tried to fill it; the test timed out.
why: Dialog or button naming differed from the test expectation; the create button label is Ok in the inline dialog.
workaround: Changed the locator to the Ok button and reran.

what: Product images: the seed uploads a generated PNG per product through the file chooser; the customer card grid and details page show the real image (placeholder only without one); the admin view shows the file name.
why: Binary upload through the generated create dialog is the documented route; display in the customer front needs the token download.

what: Seed and card tests counted 9 products instead of 8 because a Temp product left by a failed F10 run stayed in the list.
why: Tests are not isolated; leftovers of failed runs are not removed before the seed count check.
workaround: Added a cleanup of Temp products to the admin seed, like an admin would.

what: Variant test: Delete matched two buttons (page header and variants table), and the header showed Update and Cancel instead of Delete while the product had unsaved changes.
why: Generated page shows Update and Cancel in edit mode; two Delete buttons exist when a table is on the view.
workaround: Cancel first when visible, then Delete with .first(); Escape in finally to close a stray dialog.

what: Variants and addresses inside a product or profile view are saved only with the page Update button; the tests failed until they clicked Update.
why: Composed child rows belong to the parent view and are stored with the parent save; the catalog does not say so next to the inline table pattern.
workaround: Tests click Update (saveView, saveProfile) after adding the child rows.

what: Variants table hidden on the customer product view by registering a custom implementation for the variants component; the admin keeps the inline table.
why: Customers should not see variant management; the customer details layout is custom code.

what: Customer addresses list via CustomerAccount!filter(...)!any().addresses showed only 2 of 6 stored addresses.
why: Cause not found in one kb-guided try; the !any() form on the composed list returned a partial list.
workaround: Replaced with Address!filter(a | a!container(CustomerAccount).email == ...) from the container back-reference pattern; the list then showed all addresses.

what: Customer profile is a singleton CustomerAccount found by its email from the login token; addresses are a composition of CustomerAccount, listed by a container back-reference getter, so one customer sees only their own rows.
why: Ownership must be enforced in the model; the back-reference pattern avoids a stored foreign key.

what: Interceptor provisioned a CustomerAccount row for admin@example.com because the admin user also logs in through the customer client; the decision was made on the client argument and the token azp had to be used instead.
why: The client argument passed to AuthenticationInterceptor is not the client id the builder expected; the catalog does not say what it contains.
workaround: Read the azp claim, logged the origin, and returned early for non-customer clients; a stray admin row was then removed.

what: A customer who opens the back office URL gets a User not found page instead of an access message.
why: The expected error for a wrong actor is not described in the catalog as far as the builder reported.
workaround: Reported as a known behaviour in the round report; no test change.

what: Customer products access filtered with Product!filter(p | p.active) so inactive products are missing from the shop; the admin access stays unfiltered.
why: Visibility must be enforced in the access getter, not in the frontend.

what: F16 test creates two new Keycloak sign-ups on each run; the data grows and the lists are paged, so the expectations depend on earlier runs.
why: Each run adds customers and addresses; the test does not clean up or isolate them.
workaround: Used unique names per run and exact cell matches; logged as GAPS R7-9c.

what: Whole Playwright suite was not run as one command: the admin and customer modules ran separately, and the last customer test edit was not followed by an admin re-run.
why: After the module split the suite has two roots; the builder ran each one, not the whole.
workaround: Reported the split runs in the round report.

what: Keycloak first-login row insert is not done by the runtime for the managed customer actor, so custom Java was needed.
why: Documented runtime limit: managed actor auto-insert is not implemented in the current runtime.
workaround: CustomerProvisioningInterceptor in application/interceptors.

what: Category filter test on the product table was marked test.fail() in Round 6 because a relation cannot be a top-level table column or filter without a derived attribute.
why: Catalog says a RelationColumn on a top-level table is a codegen bug; a flattened derived attribute is the documented route.
workaround: Marked test.fail() with reason; the Round 7 F12 derived categoryName removed the fail and added the filter.

what: Product image: ProductImage BinaryType (PNG, JPEG, 2 MB) on Product.image; seed uploads a PNG per product; customer grid and details show it; admin shows the file name; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Variant composed in Product (label, SKU, stock), inline table on the admin product view, stored with Update; customer front hides the variants table; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: stockStatus DERIVED string (Out of stock, Low, In stock) from stock; shown in admin table and both details pages; nothing stored; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: ProductInfo.categoryName DERIVED from self.category.name; labelled Category; column and filter in the admin table; test.fail() removed; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch and F07 follow-up.

what: Customer sign-up through Keycloak registration page, CustomerProvisioningInterceptor creates the CustomerAccount on first customer login, seed script for keycloak users and realm sign-up; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Two actors: Admin (back office, /webshop/Admin) and Customer (shop front, /webshop/Customer) with their own principals, claims, accesses, menus and generated modules; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Customer products access filtered to active products (Product!filter(p | p.active)); admin access unfiltered; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Customer profile singleton by email from token; own addresses via container back-reference getter; customer 1 and 2 never see each other's addresses; commit 30914f0.
why: Level 2 batch.

what: Footwear category page lists its products in an inline table (representationComponent table on CategoryInfo View_Edit), no Products button; commit 30914f0.
why: Round 7 follow-up.
